title: Minor Odes of the Kingdom, Decade 5, Ode 2: The Hsiâo Yüan
note:
Stanzas 1 and 2 only, as Legge gives them.

Some officer in a time of disorder and misgovernment urges on his brothers the duty of maintaining their own virtue, and of observing the greatest caution.

verses.t:
Small is the cooing dove,
But it flies aloft to heaven.
My heart is wounded with sorrow,
And I think of our forefathers.
When the dawn is breaking, and I cannot sleep,
The thoughts in my breast are of our parents.

The greenbeaks come and go,
Picking up grain about the stackyard.
Alas for the distressed and the solitary,
Deemed fit inmates for the prisons!
With a handful of grain I go out and divine,
How I may be able to become good.
